parameters.content:
## Renewal reminders by text: licenses, insurance, registrations

**Who it is for:** a service business that has to keep a handful of things current to keep working: the state contractor license, liability and workers' comp insurance, the city or county business license, truck tags, the company's annual filing, bonds, the domain name. Miss one and you can end up unable to pull a permit, or working a job without coverage.

**How it works**
1. Your list lives in **Your settings**, one line each: `name | due date | repeat | note`. Dates like 2027-06-30 or 6/30/2027. Repeat is yearly, monthly, quarterly, every 2 years, every 6 months, or none.
2. Every morning at 8 it checks the list and texts you anything 60, 30, 14, 7, 3 or 1 days out, due today, or overdue. Overdue items come every day until they are handled.
3. Each line of the text has a **Done?** link. Tap it once you have renewed. A repeating item rolls forward to its next due date and a one-time item stops, so the list does not need editing every year.
4. On the 1st of each month you get a look at the next 90 days.
5. The first morning it texts you what it is tracking, and it tells you about any line it cannot read.

No database. Rolled dates and links live in the workflow's own static data, which n8n keeps while the workflow is published. If you change an item's date in the list, the list wins.

**Setup**
1. Select your Twilio credential on the two HTTP Request nodes that talk to Twilio.
2. Fill in **Your settings**: your Twilio number, your cell, your time zone, the address of your n8n (for the done links) and your list.
3. Publish it. The first text arrives the next morning at 8.

### 1. Your list
The morning schedule and a tapped done link both start here. Your settings are checked, and each line of the list becomes a dated item. A line it cannot read is reported to you, not skipped quietly.

### 2. The morning text
One text a day at most, even if the schedule fires twice. Items on a reminder day, overdue items, and on the 1st a look ahead. If Twilio will not take the text, it goes again the next morning, for up to 3 days.

### 3. Done links
Each link carries a one-time code for that item and that due date. A repeating item moves to its next date; a one-time item stops. The page says what changed and has an Undo link for a mistaken tap. A used or out-of-date link changes nothing.

### Trying it out
Add a test line due in 3 days, set the schedule to a few minutes from now and publish. One text arrives with a Done link. Tap it and read the page. Then put the schedule back to 8 AM.

Changed a setting while it is published? Publish again, or the running version keeps the old list.
